name: Python practice
covers: Rerail's own Python rules for async code, cancellation, timeouts, retries and resource cleanup.

rules.title: Python practice: asyncio.CancelledError caught or suppressed in an async def and not re-raised

caught.text:
import asyncio
import logging

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


async def download_all(client, urls):
    pages = []
    for url in urls:
        try:
            pages.append(await client.get(url))
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            logger.debug("interrupted, returning what we have")
            break
    return pages

passes.text:
import asyncio
import logging

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


async def download_all(client, urls):
    pages = []
    for url in urls:
        try:
            pages.append(await client.get(url))
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            logger.debug("interrupted after %d pages", len(pages))
            raise
    return pages


async def stop(task):
    task.cancel()
    try:
        await task
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        pass

rules.title: Python practice: an async def calls a sync helper, in any module, that sleeps, does network I/O, runs a subprocess or starts an event loop

passes.text:
import asyncio

from fastapi import FastAPI

from app.services.http import fetch

app = FastAPI()


@app.get("/page")
async def page(url: str):
    return await asyncio.to_thread(fetch, url)

rules.title: Python practice: release after an unguarded yield in a @contextmanager is skipped on error

caught.text:
import threading
from contextlib import contextmanager

_lock = threading.Lock()


@contextmanager
def exclusive():
    _lock.acquire()
    yield
    _lock.release()
